Only methods declared in candy-scriptui/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

MethodSummary

static hostArchive(): stringThe real-filesystem path of the phar archive hosting this install, or '' when this code is not running from an archive (same measured 3-arm law as the bin guards: Phar::running() inside the archive, a phar:// __FILE__ prefix, a self-naming .phar __FILE__; composer mode is always '').

find(string $name): CommandResolve a command by EXACT name only. Symfony's inherited find() additionally accepts unique prefixes, which made typo'd invocations silently EXECUTE a different command — choos Pizza Burger ran choose, confir ran confirm. On an exit-code-gating CLI that is a safety defect, not a convenience. Unknown names now fail closed with a did-you-mean that lists every plausible candidate (prefix matches first), so the suggestion also stops misdirecting.

MethodSummary

attachPump(\React\EventLoop\LoopInterface $loop): void
detachPump(): void
pid(): int
exited(): bool
wait(): int
kill(int $signal): void
exitCode(): ?int
terminate(): void
close(): int
stdout(): string
stderr(): string

stderrBytes(): string
stdoutDropped(): int

finish(int $code = 0): voidConvenience: simulate the child finishing with the given code.

Process interface

candy-scriptui re-export of the sugar-pty process contract, widened with the lifecycle surface the spin chain actually calls, so \SugarCraft\ScriptUi\Model\SpinModel, \SugarCraft\ScriptUi\Command\SpinCommand and every test double type against ONE pinned interface.

MethodSummary
drain(): voidPump both capture pipes right now, bounded and non-blocking. Cheap to call per tick: appends new bytes only.
attachPump(\React\EventLoop\LoopInterface $loop): voidRegister the capture pipes on $loop so bytes move while the run loop is alive (scriptui-02: the cure for a child blocking at the ~64KiB OS pipe buffer with nobody reading). Idempotent per loop.
detachPump(): voidUnregister the read-stream pump. No-op when not attached; every settle path calls it so watchers never outlive the loop.
terminate(): voidSignal the child (SIGTERM); does NOT reap. close() reaps.
close(): intReap the child, bounded (TERM→grace→KILL ladder). Idempotent: every call after the first returns the same code.
stdout(): stringCaptured stdout bytes (drains first).
stderr(): stringCaptured stderr bytes (drains first).
stdoutDropped(): intscriptui-03: bytes seen past the capture cap for stdout (0 when every drained byte was retained). Non-zero means the post-run print shows the head only.
stderrDropped(): intscriptui-03: bytes seen past the capture cap for stderr.

RealProcess final class

The canonical non-PTY child handle for candy-scriptui: one copy owns the whole lifecycle (spawn → drain → signal → reap) so every fix in the spin process chain lands exactly once.

MethodSummary
static spawn(array $command, bool $captureStdout = false, bool $captureStderr = false): selfSpawn a non-PTY child. $captureStdout/$captureStderr decide whether stdout/stderr land in our capture pipes (drained by drain()/stdoutBytes()) or are inherited from the parent's STDOUT/STDERR.
groupManaged(): boolWhether the tracked pid leads the child's process group (the detach wrapper was armed). True ⇒ signals go to the whole tree; false ⇒ direct-child only (the pre-scriptui-04 shape, still correct when no wrapper exists — signalling our own group would be self-harm).
pid(): int
drain(): voidBounded non-blocking pump of both capture pipes. This is the run-loop drain vocabulary: call it per tick (or per read-stream event) and a child writing past the ~64KiB OS pipe buffer never blocks waiting for a reader that only shows up after the loop ends.
stdoutDropped(): intBytes of captured stdout dropped past the capture cap (scriptui-03).
stderrDropped(): intBytes of captured stderr dropped past the capture cap (scriptui-03).
attachPump(LoopInterface $loop): voidRegister both open capture pipes on the event loop (scriptui-02, the 64KiB cure). The run loop used to poll only the exit verdict, so a child writing past the ~64KiB OS pipe buffer blocked forever while the spinner painted: nobody drained until after the loop ended. With the pump attached, every loop wakeup that sees readable pipe bytes runs drain() — the child never stalls, the parents poll keeps ticking, and EOF retires the watcher.
detachPump(): voidUnregister the read-stream pump (no-op when not attached). Called by the command right after the run loop returns and by every wait() settle path, so capture fds never outlive the loop watching them.
exited(): boolNon-blocking exit probe: reads live status while the handle is open, caches the verdict once the child is gone. Never drains or reaps — that is drain()/wait()/close()'s job.
exitCode(): ?int
kill(int $signal): voidSignal the child — its whole process GROUP when the detach wrapper armed the tree (scriptui-04), the bare pid otherwise. Libc::kill() (sugar-pty's FFI route), not bare posix_kill(): ext-posix is optional on this fleet. The exited() guard before AND after the failed call is the pid-reuse guard — signalling a reaped (possibly recycled) PID risks an unrelated process, so a post-exit kill is silently dropped instead. While the group leader (our tracked pid) lives, the group exists, so a running handle never ESRCHs.
terminate(): voidSignal the child with SIGTERM. Lifecycle split: terminate() only *signals*; close() is the sole *reaping* path and it bounds the wait (grace + SIGKILL escalation), so close-after-terminate neither double-kills nor hangs. Idempotence guards: skip when the handle was already reaped ($closed), when a SIGTERM was already sent ($terminated), or when the child already exited on its own.
close(): intReap the child, bounded. If terminate() asked the child to stop and it is still running, give it TERM_GRACE_SECONDS to honour SIGTERM, then escalate to SIGKILL — the fleet-standard TERM→grace→ KILL ladder. The grace poll drains the capture pipes as it goes: a dying child that is still writing must not wedge the window.
wait(): intBlock until the child exits, pumping the capture pipes every poll iteration, then settle the handles: final drain, close pipes, proc_close. A cached or already-reaped verdict still settles (bytes produced before the reap stay readable); a handle the closer never saw returns the cached code or -1 — NEVER a fabricated success.
stdout(): stringCaptured stdout bytes (drains first).
stderr(): stringCaptured stderr bytes (drains first).
stdoutBytes(): string
bufferedPeek(): stringZero-IO view of the buffered stdout — for pump-proof instrumentation that must observe bytes WITHOUT draining (a peek that drains would hide a broken pump behind its own polling).
stderrBytes(): string
descendantPids(): arrayThe process tree rooted at the tracked pid (direct+transient children, breadth-first), EXCLUDING the tracked pid itself and this runner. Linux reads /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children per level; elsewhere one ps -A -o ppid=,pid= helper per level does the job. A process that raced away between levels simply contributes no children — the walk must never signal pids it did not verify.
__destruct()scriptui-05 (candy-scriptui-035): the zombie-reaper safety net, mirroring sugar-pty's PosixChild::pollDestruct policy — an already exited child gets its zombie reaped and its handles let go when the object dies without close(); a still-running child is NOT signalled from a destructor (destructors must not throw, and killing a live tree during GC could fire long after the owner stopped intending it). The command-level finally ladder is the real guarantee; this only cleans the process-table residue of abandoned handles.

SugarCraft\ScriptUi\Runtime

ColourGate final class

Resolves the colour capability for non-interactive output from the standard negotiation family (NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE / FORCE_COLOR / TERM=dumb) plus the global --ansi / --no-ansi flags, and pins it as sugar-style's ambient profile so every Style minted afterwards — flag-built styles, log badges, and the sugar-markdown theme styles used by format — renders inside the resolved tier instead of emitting escapes the terminal would ignore.

MethodSummary
static cap(?InputInterface $input = null): ColorProfileThe narrowest colour capability in force for this invocation. ColorProfile::TrueColor means "no restriction".
static ladder(): ColorProfilescriptui-35 (finding 055): when no gate variable decides, believe the terminal's own advertisement instead of assuming TrueColor — TERM=screen / vt100 used to receive CSI 38;2;… they ignore. Delegates to sugar-core's TERM/COLORTERM ladder with NO tty probe: a pipe still carries styled bytes (see the class note), it is only the terminal FAMILY that narrows the tier.
static termIsDumb(): boolscriptui-36 (finding 111): ONE shared dumb-terminal predicate over TERM — unset, set-but-empty, or literally dumb. termenv treats all three as dumb-equivalent; the old two sites each eyeballed === 'dumb', so a TERM='' session skipped both the colour route and the MODE posture and shipped DEC-private bytes into an environment that never advertised them. Both the colour ladder above and InteractiveRuntime::programOptions() now consume this.
static install(?InputInterface $input = null): ColorProfileResolve the capability and pin it as the process-ambient profile for every Style::new() created afterwards. Returns the resolved cap so callers (tests) can assert it.
static clamp(ColorProfile $requested, ?ColorProfile $ambient = null): ColorProfileClamp a requested profile to the ambient capability: styles that pin their own (higher) tier — e.g. a parsed 0-15 index claiming Ansi — must not re-widen colour past a gate that says Ascii.
static resetAmbient(): voidRestore the unrestricted ambient (test isolation helper).

CursorMode final class

The --cursor-mode vocabulary shared by the interactive text commands (input, write). gum accepts exactly blink | static | hidden and distinguishes all three: the two visible arms set the DECSCUSR cursor style (blink = blinking block ESC[1 q, static = steady block ESC[2 q, mirroring charmbracelet's cursor.Blink/cursor.Steady which program the same pair), while hidden asks the Program to hide the cursor via \SugarCraft\Core\ProgramOptions::$hideCursor (DEC private ?25l — a different mechanism, so the arms never collide). scriptui-73 (finding 099): before this row blink and static painted byte-identical frames and the documented distinction was hollow. Emission and the ESC[0 q exit reset live in InteractiveRuntime::emitCursorStyle(), gated on dumb TERM like every other DEC byte this app paints.

MethodSummary
static isKnown(string $mode): bool
static hidesCursor(string $mode): bool
static styleSequence(string $mode): ?stringThe DECSCUSR start-up sequence that gives the mode its visible meaning, or null when the arm needs no style byte: hidden is owned by the hide mechanism, and an unknown mode must not paint.

InteractiveRuntime final class

Single launch chokepoint for every interactive \SugarCraft\Core\Program run in this CLI. It owns the two pipeline contract halves gum upholds:

MethodSummary
static programOptions(bool $useAltScreen, bool $hideCursor, LoopInterface $loop): ?ProgramOptionsProgram options for an interactive run, or null when NO usable input terminal exists (pipes on both ends and no /dev/tty) — callers must then refuse with a diagnostic on stderr rather than start a Program that can only deadlock or consume piped bytes as keystrokes.
static emitCursorStyle(string $cursorMode, ProgramOptions $options): boolscriptui-73 (finding 099): paint the DECSCUSR style the chosen --cursor-mode word actually promises (blink ESC[1 q, static ESC[2 q) onto the same stream the Program will render to. Dumb TERM suppresses it — DECSCUSR is a CSI sequence a dumb terminal echoes instead of obeying, so it rides the same posture as the DEC-private modes above. hidden answers null here: the cursor hiding is ProgramOptions::$hideCursor's own DEC-private arm.
static emitCursorReset(ProgramOptions $options): voidRestore the terminal's own cursor style on exit (scriptui-73). Called unconditionally when emitCursorStyle() painted — a scripted blinking/steady cursor must not outlive the program.
static signalNotice(?bool $pcntlLoaded = null): ?stringscriptui-07 (candy-scriptui-036): the options above request signal-mapped cancellation (catchInterrupts: true), but sugar-core can only install the handler when ext-pcntl is loaded — without it SIGINT/SIGTERM take the default disposition (instant death: no 130/143 mapping, no teardown unwind). Surface that once on the diagnostic channel instead of letting the documented promise silently vanish. The returned sentence is the notice to print, or null when there is nothing to say (pcntl present, or already warned this run).
static resetPcntlWarningLatch(): voidF13-W (CI-watch 2026-11-13): reopen the once-per-process pcntl warning latch. The latch is deliberate in production — one notice per run — but it is PROCESS-wide state: on a pcntl-less host (the Windows CI arms) any earlier in-process call through warnIfPcntlAbsent() consumes it before the honesty test runs, so the test can no longer observe its own first-notice contract. This seam lets the suite start from a known latch state without weakening production: callers in src/ are held to the once-per-run guarantee exactly as before.
static isHeadless(): boolscriptui-06 (candy-scriptui-002/-005): true exactly when programOptions() would refuse — no stdout terminal, no /dev/tty, no stdin terminal — i.e. the only honest spin shape is the direct-run arm (no key reader, no renderer, no DEC-mode writer). Callers must not paper over this null with a raw-STDIN Program fallback: that is how one 0x1B byte in the child's DATA stream once became a forged ESC cancellation, and how 38 bytes of ?25l/?2027h chrome once corrupted a redirected data channel.
static paintsToStderr(): boolTrue when the UI frame will be painted somewhere OTHER than stdout — used to route pre-launch chrome (headers, prompts) onto the same stream the Program paints to.
static paint(string $text): voidWrite UI text (never result data) to the stream the interactive frame belongs on, per the paintStream() ladder. When nothing can display (every stream redirected, no /dev/tty) the text is dropped — corrupting a captured data file with chrome is worse than silence, and callers refuse the whole run in that shape anyway.
static setTerminalProbesForTesting(?array $probes): voidTest seam (scriptui-34): fabricate the terminal-shape census without a real controlling terminal — keys setTerminalProbesForTesting() to null restores the honest probes.
static stdoutIsTerminal(): bool
static stderrIsTerminal(): bool
static stdinIsTerminal(): bool

TimeoutGuard final class

Wall-clock deadline for an interactive \SugarCraft\Core\Program run.

MethodSummary
static arm(LoopInterface $loop, float $seconds, \Closure $onFire): selfSchedule a one-shot deadline on $loop. When $seconds > 0 the timer flips fired() and invokes $onFire (typically fn () => $program->kill()) exactly once. When $seconds <= 0 the guard is inert — no timer is registered and the run is never interrupted.
fired(): boolTrue once the deadline elapsed and $onFire ran.
static tryParseSeconds(mixed $raw, float &$seconds): boolStrict parse of a --timeout option value into armable seconds.
disarm(): voidCancel a still-pending deadline. Safe (and cheap) to call after the timer already fired, when the guard was never armed, or more than once — the guard forgets its timer either way, so this is idempotent.

SugarCraft\ScriptUi\Style

StyleBuilder final class

Builds a \SugarCraft\Style\Style from CLI flag values. Pure (no IO) so commands can unit-test the mapping.

MethodSummary
static fromFlags(array $flags): Style
static parseColor(string $v): ColorAccept hex (#ff8000 / #f80), 0-15 ANSI palette indices, 0-255 256-colour palette indices, or the 16 canonical palette names (red, bright-blue, …).
static parseColorWithProfile(string $v): arrayLike parseColor() but also returns the narrowest ColorProfile the input requires: - hex / 6-digit / 3-digit → TrueColor - palette index 16-255 → Ansi256 - palette index 0-15 or a name → Ansi
static parseHexColor(string $v): ColorParse a hex colour (#ff8000, ff8000, #f80, f80), expanding the 3-digit CSS shorthand to 6 digits. Any other digit count is rejected with a message naming the offending value — before this existed, inputs like #1234 fell through to a generic "unrecognised color" error.
static frameRows(array $flags): intVertical chrome rows a flag-set adds OUTSIDE the content: border top+bottom (a configured border occupies rows even when hidden — that vocabulary is a placeholder posture, not an absence), plus the vertical margin and padding sides. scriptui-26: the pager subtracts this from its auto height so a themed frame never grows past the screen (the --height/--width contract stays CONTENT dimensions).
static parseSides(string $raw): array
